description: A minimalist Android app that lets you send pre-defined mood emojis to close friends and family in real time. Built in 7 days as a personal challenge to ship a finished product from scratch. Features Google authentication, friend requests, and live emoji updates via Firebase.
subtitle: A minimalist Android app for sharing mood emojis with close friends in real time
highlights: Built **Google authentication** and friend request flows for private social connections
Implemented live emoji updates with **Firebase** for instant real-time syncing
Shipped the app in **7 days** as a focused solo challenge

description: A smart job application tracking system built on n8n that automatically monitors your Gmail inbox for job-related emails. Each incoming email is classified by a locally-hosted Mistral model (via Ollama) into categories — rejection, interview invite, follow-up, or other, extracting the company name, role, urgency, and suggested next action. Results are logged automatically to a Google Sheet, building a live dashboard of your entire job search with zero manual entry. A Telegram notification is sent instantly for every update, keeping you informed on the go. Built with n8n, Gmail, Ollama, Google Sheets, and Telegram, entirely self-hosted and privacy-preserving. This workflow eliminates the chaos of job hunting, giving you a clear, organized view of your applications and next steps, all without lifting a finger.
subtitle: Self-hosted job application tracker that classifies emails and updates a live Google Sheets
highlights: Classifies incoming Gmail emails with a local **Mistral** model via Ollama
Automatically logs status updates to **Google Sheets** and notifies via Telegram
Built to keep the job search organized with **zero manual entry**

description: The Adaptive ControlNet project presents an efficient reproduction and enhancement of the ControlNet framework, aimed at democratizing controllable synthesis. Built on Stable Diffusion v1.5, the model uses Canny edge detection for fine-grained spatial control. This work introduces adaptive gating—an MLP mechanism learning layer-specific weighting via diffusion timestamps—and a CNN-based confidence estimator for signal modulation. Trained on an RTX 3080 with 118K COCO images, the model achieved sudden convergence at approximately 21,000 steps. Results show a Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) of 28.34, outperforming the 37.83 baseline. Crucially, the architectural enhancements improved conditioning fidelity by 15.6% (0.3713 to 0.4294), validating that learned per-layer importance significantly improves structural preservation. This confirms that advanced spatial conditioning can be iteratively improved and trained effectively on consumer hardware using limited resources.
subtitle: Reproduced and extended Stable Diffusion 1.5 with per-layer adaptive gating — trained on FAU HPC
highlights: **Adaptive gate mechanism** — per-layer MLP conditioned on diffusion timestep and block depth, learning how much control signal to apply at each UNet layer
**Conditioning confidence estimator** — lightweight CNN that modulates the gate signal based on estimated control map quality
Trained on **118K COCO images** using Canny edge maps as control signal on FAU's HPC cluster (SLURM)

description: Backup Cluster Manager is an MVP for managing distributed backup nodes in a cluster environment. It combines an Angular frontend with a reactive Spring Boot backend, PostgreSQL persistence, and Docker-based multi-node orchestration. The project also includes Prometheus/Grafana monitoring and k6-based stress testing for backup create, read, and delete workflows.
subtitle: Distributed backup cluster management with monitoring and stress testing
highlights: Reactive Spring Boot backend for cluster-manager and node interactions
Angular frontend for backups, users, permissions, clusters, and tasks
Built-in observability and stress-testing with Prometheus, Grafana, and k6

ours.label: Cluster test mode
ours.value: CM + multiple nodes + monitoring + stress tests

description: Python based project which is an AI chatbot and image generation tool. The chatbot is powered by Gemma3:1b model from ollama and the image generation is done using Stable Diffusion model. The main motive of the project is tool to showcase ControlNet functionality with Stable Diffusion model. The project is a work in progess and the main focus is to create a full stack application with a web interface to interact with the chatbot and image generation tool. The project also includes features like chat history. The backend is build with FastAPI and SQLalchemy and the frontend is yet to be developed. This project uses the least resources possible to run the models locally on a machine with decent hardware.

Docker based tool to process multiple videos concurrently with predefined profiles, custom operations, and workflow automation. This tool leverages FFMPEG to perform various video processing tasks such as format conversion, resolution adjustment, and bitrate modification. Users can define profiles for different processing needs and apply them to batches of videos, streamlining the workflow and saving time on repetitive tasks. CLI and web interface options are available for user convenience. Batch processing capabilities allow users to handle large volumes of videos efficiently, making it ideal for content creators, video editors, and media professionals.

A python based project that utilizes Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to generate synthetic chest X-ray images for pneumonia detection. The project aims to augment existing medical image datasets by creating realistic synthetic images that can be used to train and improve machine learning models for pneumonia diagnosis. By leveraging GANs, the project seeks to address the challenges of limited data availability in the medical field, ultimately enhancing the accuracy and reliability of pneumonia detection systems. The generated images can help in training deep learning models, leading to better diagnostic tools for healthcare professionals. This was part of my Bacherlor's project, where I worked with 4 team members to develop this solution. Later, a research paper was published based on this project.

ControlNet Revamp is an in-development diffusion-model project focused on training an attention-augmented UNet for image generation experiments. The current version works with a 25k subset of the Fill50k dataset and implements timestep noise scheduling, training, validation, checkpointing, and sample generation. This project is an active foundation toward a broader goal: recreating the full ControlNet architecture in future iterations.
subtitle: An in-progress attention UNet diffusion project evolving toward full ControlNet recreation
highlights: Current implementation trains an attention-based UNet on a 25k image subset
Includes validation, checkpoint saving, generated sample exports, and metric tracking
Planned future work is to expand this into a full ControlNet architecture recreation

description: This project builds and evaluates a handwritten digit classifier on the MNIST dataset using two approaches: a manual neural network implementation and a PyTorch-based MLP. It covers the full pipeline from loading raw IDX binary files and preprocessing images to training, validation, testing, and error analysis. The notebook is designed as a learning project to understand forward pass, loss computation, backpropagation, and SGD optimization.
subtitle: MNIST digit classification with manual NN and PyTorch MLP
highlights: Loads raw MNIST IDX binary files without external dataset loaders
Implements a neural network manually to show forward and backward pass mechanics
Compares manual training with a cleaner PyTorch MLP implementation

description: Map App is a full-stack location platform that lets authenticated users create, browse, and manage markers on an interactive Mapbox map. The backend is built in Go with Gin and PostgreSQL, while the frontend is built in Next.js with React and Tailwind. It includes role-based access control, marker approval workflows, business menu items, discounts, tile views, and an Ollama-powered chat assistant that can operate globally or as a marker-specific customer-service persona.
subtitle: Interactive map with marker workflows, business menus, approvals, and AI chat
highlights: Role-aware marker management with USER, BUSINESS, and SUPERUSER permissions
Marker-specific AI assistant for shops, services, and events using Ollama
3D Mapbox visualization with building-aware marker placement and focus flows
